sections.mainTitle: Your pace, your race, your time

about.title: What is Pitmydoro?
about.description:
Pitmydoro is a focus timer inspired by Formula 1, designed to help you achieve your tasks and goals.



It works perfectly on both desktop and mobile, and its purpose is to help you stay focused whether you're studying, writing, coding, or planning your next goal.



Make the most of the Pomodoro method combined with F1 to make focus more dynamic and motivating.
about.title2: How does the Pomodoro technique work?
about.description2:
The Pomodoro Technique is a time management strategy that divides work into high-focus intervals, typically 25 minutes, followed by short breaks.



In Pitmydoro, each task is part of your race strategy. Each Pomodoro is a lap, and depending on the intensity of your work, you can choose between different "tires": soft, medium, hard, intermediate, or wet, adapting to the conditions of your day.



You can configure the duration of each tire and choose your favorite team to personalize your environment (This can be done from the Settings section).



Short and long breaks are your pit stops, essential to keep you on track and performing at your best.
about.title3: How to start using the Pomodoro technique?

list.1: Add the tasks you need to complete.
list.2: Assign how many pomodoros you think each task will need.
list.3: You can select a specific task to start with.
list.5: Repeat the intervals until you complete 4 pomodoros (or the number you configured).
list.6: Each time you finish a session, take a short break.
list.7: After completing 4 pomodoros, take a longer break.
list.8: Repeat the process until all your tasks are done.

hero.title: Formula 1, explained for beginners
hero.subtitle: Everything you need to start watching and actually understand what's going on — the championship, the race weekend, pit stops, tires, and the language fans use.
hero.intro: Formula 1 (F1) is the highest class of international single-seater racing. 11 teams and 22 drivers travel the world across a season, racing on circuits that range from city streets to purpose-built speedways.

championship.title: How the championship works
championship.body: A season runs roughly from March to December and is made up of many races called Grands Prix. Points scored at each race add up over the year toward two separate titles.

drivers.title: Drivers' Championship
drivers.body: Awarded to the individual driver with the most points at the end of the season. This is the title that crowns the World Champion.

constructors.title: Constructors' Championship
constructors.body: Awarded to the team. Both of a team's cars score points and those points are combined, so prize money and prestige are tied to this standing.

weekend.title: The race weekend
weekend.intro: A Grand Prix is more than just Sunday's race. A typical weekend is spread across three days:

practice.title: Practice
practice.body: Free Practice sessions (FP1–FP3) let teams test car setups and let drivers learn the track. No points are awarded.

qualifying.title: Qualifying
qualifying.body: A timed shootout split into three parts (Q1, Q2, Q3) that decides the starting order — the 'grid'. The fastest lap earns pole position, the very first place on the grid.

sprint.title: Sprint (some weekends)
sprint.body: A short, flat-out race held on selected weekends. It has its own shorter qualifying and awards a handful of points of its own.

race.title: The Grand Prix
race.body: The main event on Sunday. Drivers start from their qualifying positions and race a set number of laps. First across the line wins.

raceLength.title: How long is a race?
raceLength.body: A Grand Prix covers the number of laps needed to exceed 305 km (about 190 miles) — Monaco is the famous exception at around 260 km. Races also have a maximum running time of roughly two hours (three hours total including stoppages). In practice that means about 50 to 70 laps depending on the circuit.

rules.title: Basic rules and scoring

points.title: Points
points.body: The top ten finishers score points on this scale:

rules.fastestLap: In seasons that award it, one extra point can go to the driver who sets the fastest lap of the race, as long as they finish in the top ten.

flags.title: Flags
flags.intro: Marshals wave colored flags to talk to drivers. Hover or tap each one to see what it means:

green.name: Green
green.meaning: Track is clear — racing or the session resumes normally.

yellow.name: Yellow
yellow.meaning: Danger ahead. Slow down and no overtaking.

doubleYellow.name: Double yellow
doubleYellow.meaning: Greater danger; slow down significantly and be ready to stop.

blue.name: Blue
blue.meaning: A faster car is behind — let the leaders lap you.

red.name: Red
red.meaning: Session stopped. All cars return slowly to the pits.

yellowRed.name: Yellow & red stripes
yellowRed.meaning: Slippery surface ahead — oil, water or gravel on track.

white.name: White
white.meaning: A slow vehicle is on track ahead.

black.name: Black
black.meaning: A driver is disqualified and must return to the pits.

chequered.name: Chequered
chequered.meaning: The session or race is over.

penalties.title: Penalties
penalties.body: Breaking the rules — speeding in the pit lane, causing a collision, repeatedly exceeding track limits — can bring time penalties, grid drops, or in serious cases disqualification.

raceControl.title: Race control: neutralizing the race
raceControl.intro: When there's danger on track, race control slows everyone down instead of stopping the race outright:

safetyCar.title: Safety Car (SC)
safetyCar.body: A real car comes out to lead the field at reduced speed, bunching everyone together. Overtaking is banned until it pulls in and racing resumes.

vsc.title: Virtual Safety Car (VSC)
vsc.body: No physical car: instead, every driver must hold a delta — a slower target time — all the way around the lap. It's used for smaller incidents that don't need a full Safety Car.

intervals.title: Intervals
intervals.body: The time gaps between cars, shown in seconds on the timing screens. Watching the interval tells you whether a chasing driver is closing in or dropping back.

pitstops.title: Pit stops
pitstops.body: During the race, cars stop in the pit lane so the crew can change tires and make small adjustments. A modern pit crew of around twenty people can swap all four wheels in roughly two to three seconds. A stop is effectively mandatory in dry races because the rules require each driver to use at least two different tire compounds.
pitstops.why: Strategy lives here: when you stop, and which tires you fit, can win or lose a race.

tires.title: Tire compounds
tires.intro: Tires are at the heart of F1 strategy. The supplier brings dry-weather 'slick' tires in different compounds, plus two types for rain. Softer rubber grips better but wears out faster; harder rubber lasts longer but offers less grip.

medium.name: Medium
medium.use: An all-round compromise between speed and life

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.use: A damp track or light rain

tech.title: The 2026 car: active aero & overtake mode
tech.intro: For 2026 the rules changed dramatically and DRS was retired. Two new tools take its place:

activeAero.title: Active aerodynamics
activeAero.body: Front and rear wings now move automatically between a high-downforce mode for the corners and a low-drag mode on the straights, making the cars faster and far more efficient.

overtake.title: Manual Override (overtake mode)
overtake.body: A push-to-pass style burst of extra electrical power a chasing driver can deploy to help attack the car ahead — the modern, battery-powered replacement for DRS.

teams.title: Teams and how they're built
teams.body: F1 is contested by constructors — teams that design and build their own cars. Each team enters two cars, so the size of the grid is simply the number of teams times two.

season2026.title: A bigger grid for 2026
season2026.body: 2026 marks a new era: the grid grows to eleven teams and twenty-two drivers. Cadillac joins as a brand-new constructor, while Audi takes over the squad formerly known as Sauber.

roster.title: Who's in a team
roster.body: Beyond the two race drivers, a team includes a team principal who runs it, race engineers who guide each driver, strategists, mechanics, aerodynamicists, and a pit crew — often hundreds of people back at the factory.

reserve.title: Reserve drivers
reserve.body: Teams also keep reserve (or test) drivers ready to step in if a race driver can't compete.

grid.title: The 2026 grid
grid.note: Driver line-ups can still change before the season begins.

glossary.title: Speak the language
glossary.intro: A few terms you'll hear over and over:

pole.def: First place on the starting grid, earned by the fastest qualifying lap.

podium.def: The top three finishers, celebrated on a raised platform after the race.

dnf.def: 'Did Not Finish' — a car that retired before the end, usually from a crash or mechanical failure.

dns.def: 'Did Not Start' — a driver who qualified but couldn't take the start of the race.

boxBox.def: The radio call telling a driver to come into the pits ('box' comes from the German Boxenstopp).

stint.def: A continuous run on one set of tires, between the start (or a pit stop) and the next stop.

outInLap.def: The lap leaving the pits on fresh tires (out-lap) and the lap returning to the pits (in-lap).

formationLap.def: The lap before the start, used to warm up tires and brakes before cars line up on the grid.

undercut.def: Pitting earlier than a rival for fresh tires to gain time and jump ahead of them.

overcut.def: The opposite of an undercut: staying out longer on older tires while a rival pits, hoping clear track lets you leapfrog them.

pitWindow.def: The range of laps in which it makes strategic sense for a driver to make their pit stop.

slipstream.def: Following closely in another car's wake to cut air resistance and gain a speed boost on the straights.

dirtyAir.def: The turbulent air behind a car that reduces grip for whoever is following, making overtaking harder.

backmarker.def: A slower car at the back of the field, often about to be lapped by the leaders.

lockUp.def: When a wheel stops turning under heavy braking, flat-spotting the tire and usually running wide.

graining.def: A type of surface tire wear that costs grip until the rubber 'cleans up' again.

marbles.def: Bits of worn rubber that gather off the racing line; driving over them is slippery.

delta.def: A target lap time drivers must respect, for example under a Virtual Safety Car.

parcFerme.def: Conditions under which teams may no longer change a car's setup, usually from qualifying until the race.

paddock.def: The restricted area behind the pits where teams base their garages and motorhomes.

grandChelem.def: A rare feat: pole position, win, fastest lap, and leading every lap in a single race.

privacy.summary: In short: Pitmydoro stores the minimum needed to run your timer, your tasks and your statistics. Your data is never sold. You can request its complete and permanent deletion at any time.

controller.title: 1. WHO OPERATES PITMYDORO
controller.description: Pitmydoro is an independent, open source project maintained by an individual developer. It is not operated by a company and has no dedicated data protection department. All privacy enquiries are handled through the contact address at the end of this policy.

dataCollection.title: 2. WHAT DATA WE COLLECT
dataCollection.description: The App works without an account. If you choose to sign in, the following categories of data are collected:

account.title: Account data
account.description: Provided by you or by your chosen sign-in provider:
account.email: Email address, used to identify your account and to verify deletion requests.
account.profile: Display name, username, profile picture, country flag and badges.
account.tokens: Authentication identifiers and session tokens issued by the sign-in provider.

activity.title: Activity data
activity.description: Generated as you use the App:
activity.sessions: Pomodoro sessions, breaks, pauses and interruptions, with their durations.
activity.tasks: Tasks, estimates, completion state and sticky notes.
activity.stats: Daily statistics, streaks, reports and leaderboard standings.
activity.settings: Preferences such as timer durations, theme, language, sound and notification settings.

technical.title: Technical data
technical.description: Collected automatically by the infrastructure that serves the App, primarily for security, abuse prevention and diagnostics:
technical.device: Browser type, device type and operating system.
technical.network: IP address and approximate region derived from it.
technical.logs: Request and error logs, including timestamps.

dataCollection.noSensitive: Pitmydoro does not request, and is not designed to hold, special categories of data such as health, biometric, financial or government identification data. Do not enter such information, or any other sensitive data, credentials, passwords or secrets, into any field of the application, including task titles, descriptions, notes, sticky notes, profile fields, display names and any other free-text input.

purpose.title: 3. WHY WE USE IT
purpose.operate: Operate the timer, save your tasks and calculate your statistics.
purpose.account: Create and maintain your account and keep you signed in.
purpose.features: Provide features you request, such as profiles, leaderboards, reports and stream overlays.
purpose.secure: Protect the service against abuse, fraud, manipulation and security incidents.
purpose.improve: Understand how the App is used in aggregate, find points of improvement and decide what to build or fix next.
purpose.noSale: Your data is not sold, rented or traded, and is not used for advertising profiling.

access.title: 4. ADMINISTRATION AND ACCESS
access.description: Data you store in Pitmydoro is held in third-party infrastructure administered on behalf of the service. Operating, maintaining, debugging, securing and supporting the App requires administrative access to that infrastructure, which may involve access to stored records, including account and activity data.
access.scope: Such access is limited to what is necessary to run the service, investigate faults, respond to support or deletion requests, prevent abuse or comply with the law.
access.warning: By using the App you acknowledge and accept this. You should treat anything you enter as information that is stored on systems you do not control, and you are solely responsible for what you choose to enter.

processors.title: 5. SERVICE PROVIDERS
processors.description: Pitmydoro relies on third-party providers to host the application, authenticate users and store data. These providers process data on our behalf, under their own security and privacy terms, and may store it on servers located outside your country.
processors.firebase: Google Firebase (Google LLC): authentication, database, file storage and scheduled server functions. Your account data, activity data and statistics are stored in Cloud Firestore, uploaded files such as profile pictures are stored in Cloud Storage for Firebase, and background processing runs on Cloud Functions.
processors.analyticsProvider: Google Analytics for Firebase (Google LLC): optional usage analytics, active only with your consent, as described in the analytics section below.
processors.google: Google Sign-In (Google LLC): used when you choose to sign in with a Google account. Google provides your email address, name and profile picture to the App, and handles the credentials itself, which are never seen or stored by Pitmydoro.
processors.vercel: Vercel (Vercel Inc.): hosting and delivery of the application. It processes technical data such as your IP address and request logs in order to serve the site.
processors.sentry: Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.): error and crash monitoring, used to detect and fix faults in the App.
processors.policies: Each provider processes data under its own privacy policy, which governs its practices. We recommend reviewing them if you want to know how they handle data on their side.
processors.responsibility: The Operator does not control the internal practices of these providers and accepts no liability for their acts, omissions, outages or security incidents.

cookies.title: 6. COOKIES AND LOCAL STORAGE
cookies.description: The App uses cookies and browser local storage for the following purposes:
cookies.essential: Essential: keeping you signed in, maintaining your session and preventing concurrent sessions in multiple tabs. These are required for the App to work.
cookies.preference: Preference: remembering your settings, such as theme, language, timer durations and sound options.
cookies.consent: Consent: recording whether you accepted or declined cookies, so you are not asked again.
cookies.analytics: Analytics: only if you accept, identifiers used by Google Analytics for Firebase to measure aggregated usage. They are never set if you decline.
cookies.control: You may decline non-essential cookies from the banner shown on your first visit, and you may clear stored data at any time from your browser settings. Clearing it will sign you out and reset local preferences.

analytics.title: 7. ANALYTICS AND ERROR MONITORING
analytics.intro: Two optional tools help us understand how the App behaves in the real world. Neither is used for advertising, and neither is used to build a commercial profile of you.
analytics.analytics: With your consent, the App enables Google Analytics for Firebase. It records aggregated usage events such as screens viewed, features opened and sessions started, together with technical attributes like device type, browser, language and an approximate region derived from your IP address.
analytics.analyticsPurpose: Its only purpose is to find points of improvement: which features are actually used and which are ignored, where people abandon a flow, which screens fail to do their job, and which problems are worth fixing first. It tells us what to build and repair next, nothing else.
analytics.analyticsConsent: Analytics is disabled by default and is only activated if you accept cookies. If you decline, or later clear your stored data, collection stays off and the App keeps working exactly the same.
analytics.errors: The App uses Sentry to detect crashes and errors. When something fails, Sentry receives a technical report containing the error message and stack trace, the URL where it happened, the browser and operating system, and a technical identifier used to group repeated occurrences.
analytics.errorsPurpose: These reports exist solely to detect, reproduce and fix faults, and to protect the service against abuse. They are not used to track your browsing, to measure your activity or for any commercial purpose.
analytics.errorsScope: Error reports may incidentally include technical context from the page where the failure occurred. We do not deliberately send the content of your tasks, notes or profile to this service, which is another reason not to store sensitive information in those fields.

sharing.title: 8. WHEN DATA MAY BE DISCLOSED
sharing.description: Your data may be disclosed only in the following circumstances:
sharing.providers: To the service providers described above, strictly to operate the App.
sharing.legal: When required by a valid legal obligation, court order or request from a competent authority.
sharing.security: To investigate, prevent or respond to fraud, abuse or security incidents.
sharing.rights: To establish, exercise or defend legal claims.
sharing.public: Some information is public by design, including your display name, username, profile picture, badges and leaderboard position.

security.title: 9. SECURITY
security.description: Reasonable measures are applied to protect stored data, including access rules on the database and authentication handled by an established provider.
security.warning: No method of transmission or storage is completely secure. No guarantee is made that data will remain private, intact or available, and the Operator cannot be held liable for unauthorised access, loss or alteration beyond its reasonable control.

retention.title: 10. RETENTION AND DELETION OF YOUR DATA
retention.description: Data is kept for as long as your account remains active. If you stop using the App, data may remain stored until you request its deletion.
retention.deletion: You may request the absolute and permanent deletion of your personal data, account, tasks, notes, statistics and reports at any time, at no cost, by writing to <mail>{email}</mail>.
retention.requirement: For security reasons the request must be sent from the same email address associated with your Pitmydoro account. Requests sent from any other address cannot be verified and will not be processed.
retention.term: Verified requests are completed within a maximum of {days} days from receipt.
retention.irreversible: Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Deleted statistics, streaks, reports and leaderboard history cannot be recovered.
retention.exceptions: Residual copies may persist briefly in routine encrypted backups until they expire, and records may be retained where a legal obligation requires it.

rights.title: 11. YOUR RIGHTS
rights.description: Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, export, restrict or delete your personal data, and to withdraw consent. Many of these actions are available directly in the App from your profile and settings.
rights.exercise: To exercise any right that is not available in the App, write to the contact address below from the email associated with your account.

children.title: 12. CHILDREN
children.description: The App is not directed to children under 13, or under the minimum age of digital consent in your country. Accounts identified as belonging to a child below that age will be deleted.

international.title: 13. INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS
international.description: The App is operated from Mexico and uses providers with global infrastructure. By using the service you acknowledge that your data may be stored and processed in countries whose data protection laws may differ from those of your own.

changes.title: 14. CHANGES TO THIS POLICY
changes.description: This policy may be updated at any time. The revision date at the top of this page indicates the current version. Continuing to use the App after a change constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

contact.title: 15. CONTACT
contact.info: For any privacy question or to request deletion of your data, write to:
